sentences.text: Present Misc. Appeal, under Section 173 (1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for brevity "the Act") has been preferred by the appellant/Insurance Company assailing the award dated 24/10/2013 passed by Tenth Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Gwalior (M.P.) in Claim Case No.139/2013.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd vs Ashok Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The accident in question took place on 6/9/2011 in which respondent No. 3 sustained grievous hurts.

Briefly stated facts of the case are that on 6/9/2011 at 6 am when respondent No. 3/claimant was going to circle for purchasing bread and reached near Santosh Kirana Store, the respondent no.
2-driver of the offending truck by driving the truck in wrong side rashly and negligently dashed the claimant due to which he sustained grievous hurt in left paw of his leg and also sustained other injuries on other part of the body.
The FIR was lodged and challan was filed agaisnt the respondent No. 2.
Respondent No. 3/claimant had filed the claim petition under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 seeking compensation to the tune of Rs. 15,40,000/- on account of injuries sustained by him.

The Claims Tribunal vide impugned award has awarded a compensation of Rs. 4,70,348/- for the injuries sustained by the respondent No. 3 with interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum and liability for payment of compensation amount was fastened on respondents No. 1 and 2 viz. owner and driver of the offending vehicle; however, appellant/Insurance Company was directed to make the payment of compensation amount first to claimant and thereafter recover the same from respondents No. 1 and 2.

The Insurance Company has filed this appeal on the ground that while passing the impugned award Claims Tribunal failed to appreciate that incident occurred due negligence of claimant himself and therefore, claim petition itself was not maintainable.

The driver of the truck was not holding valid and effective driving license and was driving the truck in breach of policy conditions and therefore,
the Insurance Company cannot be fasned with liability whatsoever to satisfy the award.

Though ground raised by Insurance Company regarding breach of Insurance Policy was sustained; however,
learned Claims Tribunal erred while recording finding regarding pay and recover; however, after satisfying the award the chances of recovery of the amount from the respondents no. 1 and 2 is very low.
He further submitted that the income of the claimant as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is on higher side and also the interest rate as awarded at the rate of 7.5% per annum is also on higher side.
On the other hand respondent No. 3/claimant also filed cross-objections under Order XLI Rule 22 of CPC challenging the inadequacy of award amount.

It is the submission of learned counsel for respondent No. 3 that in the aforesaid incident, left paw of the respondent No. 3's leg was amputated and therefore, Claims Tribunal has erred in assessing the permanent disability at the extend of 20% and further the amount awarded under the head loss of income, medical expenses, pain and suffering, special died, attender charges is on the lower side.
It has further been argued on behalf of respondent No. 3 that claimant is also entitled for award of amount under the head future prospect in light of decision of Apex Court in the matter of National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017 ACJ 2700).

entities.text: National Insurance Company vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, (2017 ACJ 2700)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the parties at length and perused the record.

As regards grounds raised by learned counsel for the appellant/Insurance Company regarding fastening the liability to pay first and thereafter recover the amount of compensation from respondents No. 1 and 2 is concerned, in the opinion of this Court the findings as recorded by the Claims Tribunal in this regards are just and proper as it is not in dispute that offending truck was insured with appellant/Insurance Company on Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd vs Ashok Singh on 17 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/84639660/
2 the date of accident and therefore, this ground is not sustainable in the eyes of law.

entities.text: Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd vs Ashok Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
However, as regards interest rate, in the opinion of this Court award of interest at the rate of 7.5%
per annum is on higher side looking to the decision of Apex Court in the matter of Divisional;
Manager, Oriental Insurance co. Ltd., Cuttack Vs. Kalbalatha Mohaapatra, 2005 (1) TAC 569,
wherein it has been held that rate of interest must be just and reasonable depending upon the facts and circumstances of each case taking all relevant factors including inflation, change of economy and policy adopted by Reserve Bank of India and accordingly same is reduced from 7.5% to 6%.

entities.text: Manager, Oriental Insurance co. Ltd., Cuttack Vs. Kalbalatha Mohaapatra, 2005 (1) TAC 569
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As regards cross-objections filed by respondent No. 3/Claimants the amount awarded by the Claims Tribunal under the heads medical expenses, pain and suffering, special died, attender charges etc.
are just and proper and needs no interference and disability to the tune of 20% as assessed is also just and proper, however, learned Claims Tribunal erred in not awarding any amount under the head future prospects.

The Claims Tribunal has assessed the income of the injured as Rs. 8,000/- per month and after applying 20% permanent disability, the monthly loss due to permanent disability comes to Rs.
1,600/- after adding 40% towards future prospects, the monthly loss comes to Rs. 1,600 + 640 =
2240/- and years loss due to permanent disability comes to Rs. 2,240 x 12 = 26,880/- and after applying multiplier of 15 as has been applied by Claims Tribunal total loss of income due to permanent disability comes to Rs. 26,880 x 15 = 4,03,200/-, the Claims Tribunal has already awarded a sum of Rs. 2,88,000/- under the aforesaid head, therefore, now after adding future prospects, the claimant shall be entitled for enhanced sum of Rs. 4,03,200 - 2,88,000 = 1,15,200/-.

In the result, the appeal filed by appellant/Insurance Company as well as the cross-objections filed by respondent No. 3/Insurance Company vide I.A.No. 3217/2014 are hereby allowed in part and the total amount awarded to the claimant/respondent No. 3 is enhanced by a further sum of Rs.
1,15,200/- thereby, making the total compensation amount to Rs. 4,70,348 + 1,15,200 = 5,85,548/-.
The amount of award shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till its realization.
The amount of compensation shall be payable to the claimant within 12 weeks from the date of production of a certified copy of this order.
Rest of the conditions regarding liability and pay and recover as imposed by trial Court in impugned award shall remain intact.

Appeal as well as I.A.No. 3217/2014 are allowed in part and disposed of.
(ROOPESH CHANDRA VARSHNEY) JUDGE JPS/-
